sense.text:
This is spoken of America. “Behold, thou art wiser than Daniel”: Daniel could interpret dreams; America can interpret your next move, because of the surveillance and the technology it has. “There is no secret that they can hide from thee.”

So if no secret can be hid from America, according to God, how did they mistakenly hit a school in Iran and think it was part of their base? The president says he knows nothing about it. Earlier in the week they tried to say it was a mistake, one of their old records. Then they tried to blame it on Iran. It shows they are lying to you. These are crooks and liars.

And for our people who are still asleep, following behind the beast, the prayer is that you come up out of that foolishness. Some amongst us are still following the beast: a ranking man re-enlisted in the army while America is at war, knowing he will be deployed. Not everybody who got down with the purple and gold is in the right mindset. The Lord's Passover is around the corner, and around this season the purging begins: people start dropping, because the leaven has to be removed if we want the Lord to bless us.

precepts.why:
Don't listen for one second to these liars. “The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies.” They come out of the womb lying. That is all they do, and it is what they have done since the beginning.

So the same God who says no secret can be hid from them also says they speak lies from birth. What they say about that school is a lie.

sense.text:
John saw “a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.”

The seven heads are the seven kingdoms: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain. The ten horns go into the ten common markets, which is the EU, and on the military side it is NATO today. There are over thirty nations in it at this point: Belgium, Luxembourg and so on.

And upon his heads is the name of blasphemy, because that is what they do. They blaspheme against God's tabernacle, against his people, against the image of our God, our Christ, and the angels. The beast is America.

precepts.why:
Read on and it shows what that blasphemy is: “he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.”

Them that dwell in heaven are the Most High, Christ, and the angels. This is what they do: they lie against God's people and against God himself.

“And there appeared another wonder in heaven; and behold a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his heads.” Heaven here goes into rulership: who would be leading the earth, who would be the world superpower in the latter days.

The dragon carries the same seven heads and ten horns as the beast of Revelation 13, so the beast is also the great red dragon. Red is the key indicator describing who this would actually be.

Who is this great red dragon? “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.”

Then: “And after that came his brother out.” No description of Jacob, nothing, because Jacob looked just like everybody else. Everybody at that time had dark pigmentation. Esau was different, so he had to be described.

So the red dragon is Esau, and the beast ruling the earth in the last days is his: America.

sense.text: “I will tell thee the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carrieth her, which hath the seven heads and ten horns.” That is today's class, the beauty and the beast: the woman, and the beast that carries her.

“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition”: this goes into Europe, the Europeans, Great Britain.

“And they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world”. What God just said is that the Europeans, Esau Edom, do not have their names written in the book of life, all the way from the beginning. The Lord don't love everybody the same.

The only names that are written are the Israelites: you so-called blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans. That is good news, and the Most High should get a round of applause for it.
“The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sitteth.” That goes into seven kingdoms, the seven European powers already named.

“And there are seven kings: five are fallen, and one is, and the other is not yet come”. The one that is was Rome, ruling at that time. The other not yet come is Great Britain, and “when he cometh, he must continue a short space.”

Before America got its independence, who did it get it from? Great Britain. The British are coming, the red coats: those who paid attention in history class know what this goes into.

“And the beast that was, and is not, even he is the eighth”: that is the original beast, read in Revelation 12 and Revelation 13 and higher up in Revelation 17. It was not ruling while John got this revelation.

“And is of the seven”: the Americans migrated over here from England, so they are of Great Britain. “And goeth into perdition”: they are going to be destroyed.

“And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings, which have received no kingdom as yet; but receive power as kings one hour with the beast.” The ten kings are the ten common markets, the EU, and NATO on the military side. They received no kingdom of their own, but they receive power with the beast. This is an alliance that would be made, and the ringleader, at the forefront of it, is the eighth beast: the United States of America.

History shows it come to life. After World War II the Soviet Union pressed down on Eastern Europe, and in April 1949 the Western European and North American nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty and formed NATO, agreeing that an attack on one would be an attack on all. The Soviets answered with the Warsaw Pact in 1955, and it ended when the Soviet Union disbanded in 1991. The Bible is prophetic, and over the course of time it comes to life.

“These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.” All of the nations that signed that treaty have one mind: they agreed that America would be the lead, and they gave all of their power and strength unto the beast.

But now there is conflicting interest. With the Strait of Hormuz closed in the war with Iran, France and Italy are negotiating with Iran for their own ships to pass. Canada says it will never take part. Germany warns against an endless war. Spain has permanently withdrawn its ambassador from Israel. Yes, they agreed to give America power, but in this situation they are looking out for Europe. This is your war, Trump, they say.

precepts.why:
“So he carried me away in the spirit into the wilderness: and I saw a woman sit upon a scarlet coloured beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.”

This woman goes into that well-favoured harlot. She sits on the Hudson River: a representation of America. Her skirt is being pulled and people are seeing that she is not a virgin: she is not who she portrays herself to be.

sense.text:
What was read before is that all of these kings, all of these kingdoms, agreed to give their power to the beast, the United States of America. But things are changing. “And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore”: the Lord is letting us know that something, or some things, over the course of time will cause these kings to begin to hate America.

Trump has badmouthed NATO time and time again: they're not paying their fees, he's going to end the alliance. He is very prideful. Now with Iran they say they don't want to be drawn into a long war; they're thinking about the oil prices and the destabilizing of the region. They are thinking long-term, and now in Europe they are calling for a United States of Europe.

“And shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.” How are they going to do that? With intercontinental ballistic missiles.

But before that comes, here is what we have to achieve: abstinence, discipline, overcoming, and unity.

precepts.why:
As Israelites, the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans scattered abroad, not just here in America, when we see things like this we have to understand that our salvation is getting closer. “Knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed”: nearer than when we first came to the knowledge. Things are escalating rather quickly, and this conflict is something to keep our eyes on.

A lot of us don't recognize what the feast of Passover is really about: the destruction of our enemies, and us being saved from the hands of our enemies. How fitting is that high holy day at a time like this.

So we have to increase our focus and buckle down. We are in the midst of war, and our minds shouldn't be other places. As Deacon Yashua said last Sabbath, the prophecy should move us to correction; it is not for our entertainment.

Before the ten horns turn on her, we need unity. “Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”. The nation not desired is us. They call us minorities, they put labels on us, blacks, Hispanics, and derogatory terms wherever we're at: the Dalits in India, the Afro-Iranians, the Afro-Palestinians. Wherever we're scattered we are hated and despised. But the Bible says gather together. It is all about Israelite unity, and that is what they have always feared, because if the Israelites unify together, that's the end of this wicked regime.

That is why they lie. They try to say Iran is the present-day Amalek, when Benjamin Netanyahu and his crew, the Israelis, are the Amalekites according to the Bible. To deflect that fact and that history, they say the Iranians, who are the Persians, are Amalek. Netanyahu even invoked Purim. But Purim is Esther and her uncle Mordecai, who would not bow to Haman, an Amalekite, Esau Edom, who wanted to eradicate all of our ancestors; and the Lord put the spirit on Hadassah to move the Persian king's heart so we could be free. Calling the Persians Haman is historically inaccurate.

“Before the decree bring forth”: it was already decreed, already prophesied that this will happen. Destruction is coming, so we take heed, acknowledge it, and get ourselves right.

This is the decree. “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise”: what the Lord said is going to happen is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord doesn't want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he won't put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. That is possible by nuclear fire. “The earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up.”

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? Not the ones with the popcorn just watching. Eating popcorn ain't a sin, but if all you're doing is watching and not applying, that's when it becomes an issue. This is not the time to kick our feet up or be bugging out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before, and to increase in righteousness.

sense.text:
The Lord is doing his job; it's time for us to do our job and put our focus on overcoming the beast. It doesn't matter if you live in the States or not: the United States of America is the world superpower and influences the whole world. Whatever music is played in America, whatever is in pop culture, the whole world responds to it. But this regime, this power, will fall. Thus saith the Lord.

“For the things which are seen are temporal”: the things we see now are temporary, not going to last forever, so there's no need for us to get caught up in the things of the world. “But the things which are not seen are eternal.” We don't see the kingdom right now, but the Lord is letting us know it is going to last forever.

So we stack our bricks. We can't be situational Israelites. We have to move in the spirit, knowing that our eternal home awaits us.

precepts.why:
“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”: anybody who's in this war against evil is not going to entangle himself with the affairs of this life, “that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.”

The one who chose us is our Lord and Saviour, Jesus the Christ, to be soldiers in his military. When Ezekiel saw that exceeding great army, he saw purple and gold: who else is out there as foot soldiers, going nation to nation, island to island, land to land, teaching the word of God? That's not to boast. It's the reality of it.

It's a spiritual battle, a spiritual war. “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”. We are new creatures in Christ, so the mindset has to change: the things that used to trip us up so often and so easily in the world can't any more.

sense.text:
If you feel that Satan is rising up his head against you, if you feel that old man coming back, you have to do any and everything to deaden that spirit. Now ain't the time for that. “Let us lay aside every weight”: everything that is trying to keep us from serving our God, “and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us”.

We're not worried about that war over there; God already has that. We need to worry about the war of the day-to-day. We don't have a lot of time left, so now is high time to wake up out of sleep and fight this battle right here.

precepts.why:
That weight is exactly what sin does: it presses you down from trying to please the Lord. “For the corruptible body presseth down the soul, and the earthy tabernacle weigheth down the mind that museth upon many things.” The earthy tabernacle is our flesh. We were born in sin and shapen in iniquity, so we have to understand the condition of the battle: we're going to fight against our flesh until we die or until Christ returns.

A lot of people coming into the truth think things are just going to go away. Some things you stop doing: eating pork, breaking the Lord's Sabbath, going without fringes, shaving your beard. You start keeping the commandments, your reasonable service. But hatred, lust and covetousness you may learn to cope with, and they don't go away. You have to prove to the Lord that you're able to keep that negro in check, that Latino in check.

This kingdom will go down; it's going to pass away just like everything else. “And they that use this world, as not abusing it”: you can use the things of this world, but don't get caught up, don't hit the snooze button, don't lean to the things of this world over Christ. “For the fashion of this world passeth away.”

If we really believe this Bible, we know that, and that fear should kick in. It shouldn't take someone always having to check you.

When you start walking in this truth, you have to check yourself: you should become skilful in the word of God. “Wisdom raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding standing, and exalteth them to honour that hold her fast.”

If wisdom is walking with you, if Christ is in you, by default you become skilful: skilful in the word of God, skilful in how to apply wisdom in certain situations. And wisdom exalts her children. You're embodying Christ, embodying that wisdom, and everybody will be able to see wisdom walking with you.

sense.text: Right now the Lord is giving us the place, the time and the opportunity to get ourselves right, but the day of the Lord is approaching regardless. “I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve, yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth.” The Lord knows who is who; it's not our job to do that. The Lord is going to send his angels, and they're going to sift and let it be known: that's an Israelite, that's not, that's a tare right there.

“All the sinners of my people shall die by the sword”: all the sinners that are Israelites, God's own people. That's what God said is going to happen, and there is nothing you can do to delay or undo what the Lord has already said.

“Which say, The evil shall not overtake nor prevent us.” Some have that spirit on them: I'm an Israelite, I ain't got to worry about this, I ain't ever going to overcome my sin, the Lord is going to give me mercy. We can't roll in that mentality. If you fall, get back up immediately, because this is the future for those who have that mindset.

We have to come out of the beast, out of that mentality. “Flee out of the midst of Babylon”. There may come a day when it is physical: some of us will be exiles, some of us will be deported, and sometimes you may have to go to the next city or somewhere else to keep this gospel moving. But it is also talking spiritually: flee out of the ways of the beast.

“And deliver every man his soul”: that's the real you, underneath this sinful flesh. We can't be like Lot's wife, holding on to the things we're accustomed to here; she became a part of the Lord's sacrifice. And the Lord just said all the sinners of his people will die by the sword.

These are the things to meditate on constantly. We are in the midst of war, and we ain't talking about the conflict in Iran: we are in the midst of a spiritual war right now. So we get our minds right and keep that focus, steadfast until the end.

This speaks to America's influence on our people. “Speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy”: that's why the bishops and the deacons always go into prophecy. We need to hear it, not for the entertainment, but to know the reality of it: it's either salvation or destruction, depending on what you do in this lifetime.

“For they are faithful and true”: if the Lord said it's going to happen, that's exactly how it's going to come to pass.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee.” Whoever tries to discredit this truth, don't let it trouble you. Of the prophecies heard since coming into this truth, about 80 percent have come to pass, and we're waiting for the rest. In 2018 our leadership said, watch, they're going to change the doctrine, and before you know it they'll be saying it's all right to eat this on the Passover. That is exactly what happened, because the Lord is dealing with them.

So be patient, and don't let anybody sway your faith. You've seen it before; you're just going to wait, because this is faithful and true. And we're going to have haters: that's how you know you're doing what's right.

“For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Disloyal brothers and sisters, focus sharply on that. Some say, I'm not unfaithful to God. But you're unfaithful to your brother, and that is not different: how else are you going to show your loyalty to God but through his people? The brotherhood, the unity, the loyalty. The scripture says we have to come together, and now is not the time for backstabbing and bitterness.

“I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” “For wickedness hath exceedingly polluted the whole earth, and their hurtful works are fulfilled.” How did wickedness pollute the whole earth? Esau. In the first chapter of Malachi Edom is the border of wickedness, and since the time of the Greeks that wickedness has grown and grown.

precepts.why:
“And after his death they all put crowns upon themselves; so did their sons after them many years: and evils were multiplied in the earth.” This is after the death of Alexander the Greek.

That is how wickedness polluted the whole earth: from the time of the Greeks all the way up until today evils were multiplied. The Greeks, the Romans, Spain, France, Germany, Great Britain, Russia, and the United States of America.

The earth as we know it is under much wickedness, in gross darkness. “Arise”: awake to righteousness, wake up out of that deep sleep. “Shine”: go teach, let your light shine, teach God's commandments. “For thy light is come”: our light is Christ, “and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.”

“For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth”: that goes into the nations. Every nation on the face of the earth is affected by the United States of America, by Edom; this whole world is defiled because of this nation. “And gross darkness the people”: whose people? God's people. Because of that, the Israelites have been affected.

“But the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” He is still going to choose Israel and still have mercy on his people: the ones who want to stop sinning, not the ones who take advantage of God's grace and mercy.

sense.text:
“How much she hath glorified herself, and lived deliciously, so much torment and sorrow give her: for she saith in her heart, I sit a queen, and am no widow, and shall see no sorrow.” America really thinks it's never going to have to pay for its crimes. If you're sitting like it says in Amos 9:10, thinking no harm is going to come to you, you have that same characteristic as Esau Edom.

If we want deliverance, why would we have that mentality? We can't get salvation unless they are destroyed, so if you want to remain in your sins, you want America to continue.

This is a gut check for the brothers and sisters we barely ever see, who fade because they always have something more important than the truth. Some have embodied the characteristics of America, and it's time to shake that off. A lot of you look at America and see her as a gorgeous, beautiful woman, and you're mesmerized.

precepts.why:
“Stumble not at the beauty of a woman”: don't get googly eyes, brother. “And desire her not for pleasure”: in America you can have all types of pleasures.

You have to look at America the same way, because that's how the Lord refers to her, as a harlot. A lot of brothers fall by harlots, and just because you're not picking up a prostitute doesn't mean you ain't out there dealing with harlots. This is the mother of all harlots.

Sin is pleasurable. “This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves”. Without natural affection: some people like young minors, some people like people of the same sex. Trucebreakers: unfaithful. “Despisers of those that are good”: I don't like that brother. Why not? Every time I look up he's doing something. What, teaching the word of God? Spirits like that sit amongst us. What are we talking about? Trying to get the hell up out of here, and you're worried about some petty stuff.

“Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God.” That's a big issue, because if you love pleasure more than you love God, you start making excuses to feed into that lust, and you find yourself not around doing the Lord's work as much. When everybody asks what's wrong with that brother, it's probably because he loves his lust more than God.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter”. He wanted nothing to do with Egypt or the king of Egypt, because he knew he was an Israelite and God chose him to do a glorious work, a mighty work: to deliver his people out of captivity. Some of you say America is not that bad, and you show it by your mentality and your actions.

Moses lived it up and had status in Egypt, like some have nice jobs and status in America, so you can't say it's because of that. Moses gave it all up, “Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”.

For a season: it is temporary, only here for so long, and then comes destruction and salvation. That's the mindset we have to have. We have to be robotic and get the feelings out of it. Nobody cares how you feel; feelings don't matter. Feelings get you killed.

sense.text:
Today's class is the beauty and the beast, and this goes into that beauty. When sin takes over, you can't see clearly. “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency”: that's how they perceive her. But you shouldn't be looking at America like that. When you see the Statue of Liberty, you shouldn't be like, God bless America, feeling proud; you shouldn't be like, Lady Liberty, I love her. The hell is going on up in here? Look at the crowns on the Statue of Liberty's head and there are seven, and there are ten toes. That should make you say the Bible is a true book, spot on.

“Shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.” This place is going to be destroyed. You shouldn't be sitting there gazing and mesmerized by her pleasures when you know this place is coming to an end. Wake up! Wake the hell up!

precepts.why:
“Because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the wellfavoured harlot”: some of you are caught up there. “The mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms”: they sold us; that's how we got over here. “And families through her witchcrafts.”

If you're down with America, you're down with the devil. That's what the Bible is telling us.

The prophet Nahum saw the same thing as John the Revelator. “Come hither; I will shew unto thee the judgment of the great whore that sitteth upon many waters”. All we hear about is judgment, destruction, killing with the sword: that's not something that's going to last long.

Jump down to verse 5, and it names her: “MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH.” An abomination is something the Lord hates and despises. So it's time to come up out of her.

“Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” The Lord is still sending plagues; remember the pandemic. Stay with the Lord and come up out of her spiritually, so that her condemnation is not yours.

sense.text:
“Behold, therefore I will bring strangers upon thee”: the Lord is bringing strangers upon Babylon the Great, the same one called wiser than Daniel above. Contextually it talks about the king of Tyrus, but spiritually it is prophetic about something else.

Who are these strangers? The Allahu Akbar type strangers: “the terrible of the nations”. Another word for that would be terrorist. “And they shall draw their swords against the beauty of thy wisdom”. A lot of people thought America could never be touched; the Lord is showing you otherwise. When America begins to fall, it's going to be destroyed from the inside out, and then comes the great finale with the ten horns.

“And they shall defile thy brightness”: America likes to put on as if they're righteous, playing the moral world police, while they are the ones going into countries, stealing presidents and bombing everybody.

precepts.why: A scripture can speak of a specific nation contextually and be prophetic about something else spiritually, because the Lord “would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is”. Wisdom is double: Tyrus in that day, and Babylon the Great, America, now.

sense.text:
We're in Passover season, and that is also purging season. “By mercy and truth iniquity is purged”: when you have Christ, he strengthens you to resist the sin, and iniquity is purged from you. That's why we remove the leaven, because the leaven is a representation of sin and iniquity.

To purge is to free from moral or ceremonial defilement, and our morals come from God's commandments. It is also to cause evacuation from: we need to evacuate from sin and get the leaven out of the house, because we have a deliverance we want to achieve. The Lord said remove the leaven, put the blood over the doorpost, and I'll pass over; and we were delivered from the hands of our captors.

“And by the fear of the Lord men depart from evil.” The only way we can depart from evil is that we must have fear.

precepts.why:
What are we really supposed to be scared of? Not like the man in Matthew 25 who was afraid and hid his talent, making excuses: I'm just so nervous, I'm just bashful, I don't know which decision to make. That's not the spirit of Christ; the Lord has not given us a spirit of fear.

“My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.” That is the fear the Lord is speaking of. We should be afraid of God's judgments, because he is the King of Terrors and we know what he's capable of. If we're not doing what we're supposed to do, we could come out on the wrong side of that equation.

sense.text: Going into Passover season, we focus or refocus, and get rid of the spiritual leaven known as sin. “I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.” Christ is the true vine, the root. And we are the Lord's husbandry: his plants, his trees, which in that day will become the trees of righteousness, as Isaiah said.

“Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away”. That's why we can't be like the brother who had the talent and hid it. We're the ones he planted, and if we don't bring forth fruit he's going to take away our candlestick, like it says in Revelation: you didn't do what I created you to do, so now you can't be here, because one bad apple spoils the bunch and you're going to hinder growth. So I have to take you out of the way.

“And every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.” Going into Passover, that is what it's all about: we want to keep growing in the spirit and getting closer to our Lord, our God, so we can get out of here.

“Abide in me, and I in you.” We have to stay steadfast and continue to abide in Christ: not loving our pleasures, not loving our lust more than Christ, but continuing to do the will of the Father and his Son. “As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.”

precepts.why: A vine is nothing more than a root sprouting through the ground. “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.” Christ is that root, the true vine.
The Father is the husbandman, and we are his husbandry: his plants, his trees. “For we are labourers together with God: ye are God’s husbandry, ye are God’s building.”

sense.text:
For those who are younger, pay close attention. “Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his.” We don't know who are his, but God does. And God also establishes leaders to guide you along the way, so you don't fall into the wiles of Satan, or stumble into the pitfalls and never recover yourself.

“Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity”: purge from sin, that spiritual leaven.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is Israel. Even with crops, not all of them take root. In the house of Israel there are the good ones and the bad ones.

“If a man therefore purge himself from these”: not from the gold and the silver, but from the wood and the earth. Those who are not producing fruit, those with dead spirits, those always caught up in some mess, those who separate from leaders, when the Lord established the leaders. How did you learn what the new moon was, except from a video of our leadership teaching it? Then you come in here and don't want to be around them; you want to go be with the clique in the back. The hell is this? That's the wood and the earth, and God is telling you to purge yourself from those people if you want to remain steadfast in Christ.

Then “he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work.” God can use you.

precepts.why:
“Having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence”: we have to be diligent, brothers and sisters. We can't just come in knowing that Christ is black, God is black, the angels are black. We have to add to our repertoire, add to our spirit: “add to your faith virtue; and to virtue knowledge”, and then temperance, patience, godliness, brotherly kindness and charity.

“For if these things be in you, and abound”: not just in you, but in you and growing, “they make you that ye shall neither be barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.” Then you don't have to get purged, and you don't have to worry about being taken out of the mix, because you're constantly growing and doing the Lord's will.

“But he that lacketh these things is blind, and cannot see afar off”: sin has blinded you. Things that are common sense you can't perform; you struggle constantly and never break through, because you have not purged yourself from the wrong people, and you love that pleasure more than God. You can't see that America is going to be destroyed or that salvation is coming. You're a situational Israelite living in the moment, thinking America is going to last forever. Shame.

“And hath forgotten that he was purged from his old sins.” God purged you from your old sins, but if you don't keep trimming and keep purging, you'll end up back in your old folly. This is a wake-up call, a readjustment, a punch in the gut: come up out of the foolishness.

sense.text: “It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.” She hid it, and it went on till the whole became leaven. Leaven grows.

precepts.why:
“Know ye not that a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump?” Because leaven grows, if that leaven is allowed to remain amongst other Israelites, it's going to spread and defile others.

“Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened.” We have to purge the leaven out of our own spirits and out of our congregations. “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”: so we no longer live unto ourselves; now we live unto Christ.

“Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.” Christ was warning the twelve of the leaven, and Christ was the leader. So when leaders try to warn you of leaven, you need to listen; Christ knew what he was talking about.

The disciples reasoned, “It is because we have taken no bread.” No, he was not talking about the bread: “How is it that ye do not understand that I spake it not to you concerning bread”? He was talking about their sinful nature. Don't get caught up in what they do: they say and do not; they're hypocrites. “Then understood they how that he bade them not beware of the leaven of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.”

The Pharisees and the Sadducees were Israelites. That doesn't mean we have anything against anybody, but if we see a spirit on someone that can influence us negatively, beware. The best thing to do is follow, listen, consider, and be very mindful.

sense.text:
Every year the Passover comes around and we see the same thing happen: people start bugging out, and people who've been with us see it, yet they still fall for it. We have to fight, and not play into Satan's devices. He wants you right where he's got you. Some are on their way out because they're not paying attention to class, not studying, not praying, not getting their four chapters.

“Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” We should not be ignorant of his devices, but some remain ignorant, because they despise wisdom and don't want to be taught.

precepts.why:
“He that is not wise will not be taught”. If you're a fool, it doesn't matter what somebody does for you: you're not going to be taught, you're not going to retain it.

“But there is a wisdom which multiplieth bitterness”: seeing it your own way, doing your own thing. And you're going to have a bitter end because of it.

“A stubborn heart shall fare evil at the last”: that's the bitterness. Because you're stubborn, because you don't want to learn, because when wise words come out you're in the back, or because you've got something against somebody and don't want to hear anything from them.

“And he that loveth danger shall perish therein.” People like that are very dangerous; they can get people hurt if you follow after them. They perish in their folly, unwise and not being taught, because fools despise knowledge.

sense.text:
This tends to happen every year around this time, and this is a class to wake some people up so they can get their minds right. “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God”: when you notice your study habits have changed, when you notice you're pulling back from the believers, understand that pride has set in and you are regressing, going backwards.

“And his heart is turned away from his Maker”: now that sin, that leaven, is blinding you, and you can no longer see clearly.

precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily”: how often? Daily. And the exhortation can't take place if you're not around anybody. “While it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.”

Sin may feel good, but it's a deceiver: you think you can get that feeling constantly, and you can't. The Lord said it's temporal. So stay around each other, around the righteous, daily, because if we pull away, sin can take over our mind and we may never recover. That's the scary part.

“Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: America came after the working of Satan. They make you think God is with them, but it's been the devil the whole time. It's time to come up out of the beast and separate.

“And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish”: that goes into those pleasures. You've been deceived by the pleasures of sin. “Because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved”: they love their pleasures more than God, like it said in Timothy. They despised God and opened their arms to their pleasures.

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie”. You can be deceived by sin so badly that you may never recover your soul: you'll still be alive, still living, but your soul is not there. Dead soul, dead spirit. Be very mindful.

sense.text: It's time to get control and not act off impulse, developing patience and discipline. “Seest thou a man that is hasty in his words? there is more hope of a fool than of him.” Fools are unwise; they don't want to be taught and they don't take heed to the commandments, so there's really no hope. If you're hasty and act off impulse, the Lord is telling you to consider: learn patience, resolve and discipline.

precepts.why:
Everybody should be able to see something about themselves in this class and apply it to their walk. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” Any and everybody can invade your spirit.

Because you have no discipline yourself, imagine what happens when you get around the wrong spirits: you're automatically gone. You're going to be gullible and fall for the okey-doke.

sense.text:
Stop playing the victim and gain control over our spirits. “Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey”: if we fall in our sins, we're worshipping the devil at that moment in time. Whoever we yield ourselves to obey, that's who we serve, and we can't have two masters. So we have to really consider and not act off impulse.

“Whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?” You have a choice: obey sin, or obey righteousness.

precepts.why:
Being around the righteous and staying occupied in the work helps that decision. Whoever commits sin even while around the righteous family: gosh damn, that's crazy. Satan is heavy on you.

“Whatsoever thou takest in hand, remember the end, and thou shalt never do amiss.” We have to be in that mind frame and be around the right people, so when we are tempted we can think things through, remember the judgment of the Lord, let the fear activate, and overcome.

“For as ye have yielded your members servants to uncleanness and to iniquity unto iniquity; even so now yield your members servants to righteousness unto holiness.” That's what we should do, because we came out of that darkness. Don't go back and forget that you were purged from the darkness.

And if Satan deceived you and you fell, don't think you can't get up. You can repent: that's why Christ came. Do not forget our Saviour.

sense.text:
“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God”: we have to be diligent, constantly abounding in the work, because if we don't, we can fall from the grace of God.

“Lest any root of bitterness”: if you're not occupied in doing the Lord's work, putting your hands to the plow, studying, being amongst the righteous, a root of bitterness can spring up in you, because you're not studying to combat it. You'd better rebuke that thing, and you do it by being around these people. If you draw back and separate from your people, Satan has you right where he wants you. Now he can play on your mind; when you're not constantly seeing people, you start thinking they never liked you anyway. That's what Satan does.

precepts.why: Satan wants to devour all of us. Christ told Peter that Satan desired to have him, to sift him as wheat. “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. We have to be in that mindset and know what's going on, family.

sense.text:
When you hear stuff like this, don't say, oh, that ain't it; that's just making an excuse to go back to your pleasure and your lust. “A sinful man will not be reproved, but findeth an excuse according to his will”: to feel comfortable in his lust and his pleasures.

It's like the man who picked a fight over having chicken every day, just so he could leave and go get some duck; or the co-worker the Bishop told of, who started a fight with one woman so he could go see the other. Now you're pointing the finger at everybody else, when really you want to go have fun in your pleasure and your lust. As the Bishop's graphic says, a sin-filled soul will find and make excuses only to fulfill their lust. That is very, very dangerous.

precepts.why: “A wicked soul shall destroy him that hath it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorn of his enemies.” The excuse-making, sin-filled soul destroys the very one who has it.
“Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.” We have to have fear and we have to be diligent, family, if we want to have a fighting chance.

sense.text: We have to learn discipline. “Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisdom over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances, and it pass not by my sins”. We learn discipline so we don't end up looking crazy out here.

precepts.why: “For the very true beginning of her is the desire of discipline; and the care of discipline is love”. The very true beginning of following after wisdom is the desire of discipline. So we have to fight temptation, fight off the devil, and overcome the beast in order to learn that discipline.

“Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.” We have to put on all of the armour. If we're not studying, we're not battling; we're just falling victim.

A child can play video games for hours and not do homework for more than a few minutes, because the game gives consequences right away and the homework's consequences are delayed. Keeping God's commandments is like that: we don't see instant gratification; it's delayed, though we are going to get the kingdom. With sin you feel that pleasure, that dopamine, right then and there, so you start loving the sin more than righteousness and wisdom. And once you've been hardened and deceived by sin, you no longer see any reason to keep God's commandments, because they don't do anything for you right then and there.

Wisdom rains down skill, and in this truth you're going to have to self-motivate. You can't wait for another man to give you a pep talk. You have to discipline your own soul if you want to make it.

“So shall righteousness hate iniquity”: we have to discipline our minds to hate iniquity. “When he cometh that shall defend him that diligently searcheth out every sin upon earth.” If we want the Lord to defend us, we have to learn to hate iniquity, to hate sin.

“Even so we in like manner, as soon as we were born, began to draw to our end, and had no sign of virtue to shew; but were consumed in our own wickedness.” The hope of the ungodly is “like dust that is blown away with the wind”, “like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.”

“But the righteous live for evermore”. You may not see it right now, but if you keep God's commandments, if you do that homework, you're going to live forever, while all the other stuff that feels good in the moment passes away. “Their reward also is with the Lord, and the care of them is with the most High”: the Most High cares for you, if you are able to hate sin.

sense.text:
We're in that Passover season, so let's get our minds right and remove the leaven. “I will hold my tongue no more as touching their wickedness”. “The innocent and righteous blood crieth unto me, and the souls of the just complain continually”: that's us, all of the murders, all of the injustice that has taken place against God's children here in spiritual Egypt.

“And therefore, saith the Lord, I will surely avenge them”: the Lord is going to surely avenge his people.

“I will not suffer them now to dwell in the land of Egypt”: this ain't talking about ancient Egypt. This is talking about a coming Egypt, the United States of America. “And smite Egypt with plagues, as before”: as before lets you know it's not the same one.

“Egypt shall mourn, and the foundation of it shall be smitten with the plague and punishment that God shall bring upon it.” When it comes, we don't want to go down with it.

“For the first author of beauty hath created them.” That real beauty is not the damn Statue of Liberty: she is no virgin, and only virgins are really beautiful. The first author of beauty is our God, and he looked at us as beautiful. That's why he refers to us as a woman.

precepts.why: “I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” Comely means beautiful, handsome. That is how the Lord looks at his people.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel”: cast down from heavenly rulership to earthly servitude. Why would he do that? Because we went off, away from the author who created us.

That's why you would look to another nation for its beauty. But God is letting you know he is the author, the creator of beauty, and the America you think is beautiful really ain't beautiful. Not just the skirt blowing: she's been worn out. You think she's beautiful, then you realize, damn, she's been with everyone on the block. You went against your God, so now, knowing that, we have to return back.

“Thou lovest righteousness, and hatest wickedness”: we have to love righteousness and hate iniquity.

“Hearken, O daughter, and consider, and incline thine ear; forget also thine own people, and thy father’s house”. Just like a marriage, sisters: the Lord doesn't want to share us with anybody else. He wants us to focus on him and him only.

“So shall the king greatly desire thy beauty: for he is thy Lord; and worship thou him.” When we get ourselves right, turn back to the Lord, love righteousness and hate iniquity, the Lord will desire our beauty, the way he created us. And we worship him and him only.

sense.text: “Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Wisdom is Christ, and wisdom lays hold of those who seek her. So how do we seek the Lord?

precepts.why:
“By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth”: the Lord is the one who sets up all of the kings and all of the princes on the earth.

“I love them that love me”: the Lord only loves those who love him. If you're not seeking him, he doesn't love you. “And those that seek me early shall find me.” In the midst of these wars and rumours of wars, we have a chance right now to seek the Lord early.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness”: riches and honour are with Christ, and durable riches are not temporary. They last forever. “My fruit is better than gold, yea, than fine gold; and my revenue than choice silver.”
What is Christ also known as? Wisdom. “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.” The wisdom that speaks in Proverbs 8 is Christ.

We have to be like King Solomon and pray for wisdom, so we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”. In Gibeon God said, “Ask what I shall give thee.” Solomon said, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, and asked, “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”.

As a youth King Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom, and “the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart”, and also “that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave him things he didn't ask for, because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek first the kingdom of heaven, and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of King Solomon's book.

“Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.” “I preferred her before sceptres and thrones”: do you prefer God's wisdom? Do you prefer the Lord over your sensual desires?

“I loved her above health and beauty”: Solomon didn't care about anything except wisdom. “I rejoiced in them all, because wisdom goeth before them”: wisdom goes before everything.

“I learned diligently, and do communicate her liberally: I do not hide her riches.” He didn't hide his wisdom. Just as the Bishop gets on us all the time, our communication should be in the scriptures.

“And refrain not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not thy wisdom in her beauty.” Don't hold back in speech when there's an occasion to do good.

Coveting after wisdom, searching after wisdom, is what we're supposed to do. That's how we should talk, and it should be on our minds at all times. Everything should always go back to the scriptures, so we converse in the scriptures.

sense.text: “If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally”: if we lack wisdom, just go to the source, to the Father in the name of the Son, Jesus the Christ.
“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” That's the key: nothing wavering. You have to believe.

precepts.why:
“For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways”: when we come into this truth we ain't right, and wisdom will walk with us in our crooked ways. “And bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline”: the Lord is going to jack us up because we ain't doing it right, but wisdom will still be there, “until she may trust his soul”.

“Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” There's no cap on the wisdom.

“But without faith it is impossible to please him”. Remember, all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness. Without Christ it is impossible to please the Father, so we have to make sure we build our faith. That's the key.
How do we build our faith? “So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.” As we see the days approaching, we have to increase our study and continue to converse in the scriptures.

sense.text: “Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.” The Lord will have mercy and pity on those who fear him: not the unfaithful, but those who fear him.

precepts.why: “Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee”: the Lord is going to fight those who fought against us. “And I will save thy children”, because wisdom exalts her children.

sense.text: “For, behold, I will bring forth my servant the BRANCH.” The Branch is Jesus the Christ.

“Upon one stone shall be seven eyes”: that goes into angels. “And I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.” That's what it pays to be faithful and diligent: the Lord will pardon our iniquity and remove it.

precepts.why:
“Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down”. “And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb”: we are going to overcome by the blood of the Lamb, so we must have faith and continue to be faithful, “and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.”

We have to love righteousness more than iniquity.

sense.text: “For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him, he is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat”: if we love him, he is our mighty protection. What type of heat? Nuclear heat. “And a cover from the sun at noon”, because the destruction comes at the noon day.

precepts.why: “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” All we have to do is be faithful and fear him, and he'll protect us from the destruction to come.
“By her he shall be covered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.” By wisdom we shall be covered from heat.

sense.text: “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.” He stands in boldness because he feared the Lord and stayed faithful.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”: when the nations see it, they're going to be troubled. “And shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation, so far beyond all that they looked for.” They won't be able to fathom what's taking place when those chariots come.

precepts.why: “Behold, he cometh with clouds”: those are his chariots. “And every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him.” Christ is returning with the multitude of angels.

“When I heard, my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the voice: rottenness entered into my bones”. Habakkuk was put in it: he felt it and he saw it. “When he cometh up unto the people, he will invade them with his troops.”

sense.text: “Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them”. That lion is Christ. “So shall the Lord of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof”: the Lord is going to fight for his people.
“As birds flying”: Christ and the angels. “So will the Lord of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it.”

precepts.why: What is the lion of Isaiah 31? “Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.” That lion is Christ.

“The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”. This is twofold: contextually it was talking about Nebuchadnezzar, but prophetically it is talking about Jesus the Christ. He's coming. “He is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.”

“And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion chased out of the wood: and I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”. The eagle is America. Christ is going to be roaring against America, bringing destruction.
